mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rose from -39.7 to -30.9 over the last three weeks, indicating a resumption of commuting and associated lunchtime/after-work shopping trips that should push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve week over week.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained PARKS mobility above +40 for three consecutive weeks indicates households have substituted outdoor recreation for indoor retail and recreation trips, which will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed relative to its pre-dip baseline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above +40 for 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS values 57.4, 44.1, 49.4 over last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even while PARKS stays above +40, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT (-45.1 to -41.7) and WORKPLACES (-34.4 to -30.9) reflects a coordinated return to in-person economic activity; when both series improve together for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC tends to rise over the following two weeks because commuting and shopping trips are complementary.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show upward movement in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stays flat despite simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined modestly from 10.7 to 8.6 over four weeks, indicating reduced time spent at home; this behavioral shift toward leaving the house should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, but only while the metro remains in a reopening regime rather than a lockdown regime.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remaining persistently below -40 for four consecutive weeks signals continued restrictions or reduced capacity on public transit, which caps the growth of RETAIL_REC because transit-dependent shoppers cannot reach retail destinations, over a 1-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 for all of the last 4 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged between -45.1 and -41.7 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite TRANSIT remaining below -40, indicating transit capacity is not a binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility turning positive (from -5.3 to +2.0) suggests normalization of essential shopping patterns consistent with a broader seasonal recovery cycle, which typically precedes recovery in discretionary retail and recreation trips within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM crossed from negative to positive between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and rising.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC stays flat, it indicates a diversion effect where households are consolidating trips into essential-only shopping, delaying discretionary retail recovery; this interaction predicts continued stagnation of RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises >3 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC changes by less than 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 3 points while RETAIL_REC moved only -0.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises meaningfully over the next two weeks despite the diversion pattern between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC being observed.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops more than 5 points week-on-week after a period of recovery, it signals a renewed policy tightening (e.g., restrictions or closures) that will spill over into reduced RETAIL_REC within one week, as both series respond jointly to the same policy shocks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week after at least one prior week of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -34.4 to -39.7 between t-3w and t-2w before later recovering
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week following a >5 point drop in WORKPLACES, indicating decoupling of the two series.
